clusters.name: Walter's move to Sorrel Valley, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter's move across the country in March 1952 to buy an apple orchard, within the year: June grew homesick and wrote to her sister Edna daily; Walter spent long hours out in the trees and distanced from June; Glen got into fights at his new school; Walter cut off from his brother Harlan after a quarrel over their father's land money; June kept to her bed for weeks that first winter; Walter and June had rows over money for new trees; by September, June joined the church choir and her letters to Edna thinned out. The shifts in functioning, relationship, and anxiety pile up over eighteen months as the family adjusted to the move and its stresses.

clusters.name: The orchard failure, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard's failure in May 1968 when a late frost took the whole crop and the bank called in the loan: Walter drank heavily most nights; he and Glen blamed each other over the loan; after the sale in October, Glen took over the family's money and the talks with the bank; Carl's asthma attacks worsened that winter; Nora began wetting the bed again in April 1969; Ida's heart trouble was found and she stopped working at the bakery; Walter stopped drinking by October and took work pruning trees. The shifts moved across the family from Walter to Glen to the children as the loss of the orchard and the move to Ridgeport rippled through, settling by autumn when Walter's functioning improved.

clusters.name: Glen's job loss at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen's job loss when the Ridgeport cannery closed in February 1975: Glen sat out of work most of that year in the truck in the yard for hours; he and Marian had loud fights at night over money; Marian took a second job cleaning offices at night; Nora stopped eating properly and lost weight that summer; she kept to her room and distanced from her mother; Walter began drinking again after six years; by March 1976 Glen started driving a delivery truck, and by June Nora was eating again and made the track team. The shifts moved through the household over more than a year, with Glen's loss of work at the centre and Nora caught in the conflict between her parents, settling as Glen found new work and Nora's functioning improved.

clusters.name: Wilma's move into Nora and Hollis's house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma's move into Nora and Hollis's house in January 1990 after selling her farm: Nora and Wilma clashed over the children's bedtimes and meals; Hollis worked late and kept out of the kitchen rows; Hollis took his mother's side; Owen had tantrums at preschool; Wilma took over Lily's care; Nora's eczema flared on both hands; Nora and Hollis had rows most nights; Marian drove over twice a week to take Nora's side; by June 1991 Wilma took a flat in town, and by August Nora's eczema cleared over the summer. The three-generational household created conflict between Nora and her mother-in-law, with Hollis caught between his wife and mother, and the children affected by the tension; the period settled when Wilma moved out.

declined.reason: This is an acute episode, not a period: the wildfire came over the ridge on August 12, 1994, the family slept three nights in the school gym, and they were allowed home on August 15 with the house untouched; everyone was calm again within days, with the children back at school that week by August 16. The shifts belong to a real external threat that resolved quickly, not a deepening family process.
